summary: Working in philosophy and other fields, Hermann Bonitz studied at the University of Leipzig (~1830–1834) and under Friedrich Adolf Trendelenburg at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1834–1836). He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1849–1867) and the Prussian Ministry (~1867–1888).

An Indologist and linguist, Hermann Brockhaus completed his Ph.D. at Leipzig and studied at Göttingen and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel and Christian Lassen. He was a professor at Jena (1839–1841) and Leipzig (1841, 1848, 1872–1877).

Active in Indology and linguistics, Hermann Brunnhofer studied at Bonn, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Zurich (Ph.D. 1861–1871). He worked at Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek (1873–1888), Saint Petersburg State University (1891–1901), and the University of Bern (1901–1914).

Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig (1859–1862, Ph.D.) under Hermann Brockhaus and Georg Curtius. He taught at Thomasschule zu Leipzig (~1864–1904) and Gymnasium Zwickau (1887).

An Indologist and linguist, Hermann Collitz studied at Göttingen (Ph.D.) under August Fick, Berlin, and Halle (Habilitation). He taught Sanskrit at Halle (1885), was Associate Professor at Bryn Mawr (1885–1907), and held a chair at Johns Hopkins (1907–1928).

Hermann Diels worked in philosophy, history/archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1866–1868) and under Hermann Usener at the University of Bonn (~1868–1870), later holding a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1882–1922).
Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1875–1880) and served as a professor at the University of Giessen (~1898–1922).

Specializing in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies, Hermann Ethé studied at Greifswald, Leipzig (Ph.D. 1863–1865), Munich, and Oxford. He catalogued manuscripts at the Bodleian Library (1872) and became Professor of Oriental Languages at Aberystwyth University in 1875.

An Indologist and linguist, Hermann Friedrich Mögling studied at the University of Tübingen (~1829–1834) and the Basel Mission Seminary (1834). He served as a teacher and preacher with the Basel Mission from 1838 to 1852.

Hermann Fränkel studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, Bonn, and Göttingen (~1910–1915) under Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff. He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1920–1935) and Stanford University (~1935–1953).

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Hermann Goetz studied at Munich (Ph.D.) and Leiden under Jean Philippe Vogel. He held positions at the Baroda Museum (1939–1953), National Gallery of Modern Art (1953–1955), and Heidelberg University (1961–1976).

Active in Indology, linguistics, and other fields, Hermann Grassmann studied at Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher and August Boeckh. He taught at the Ottoschule (1836–1842), Friedrich-Wilhelms-Schule (1843–1852), and Marienstiftsgymnasium (~1842–1877), where he became professor in 1852.

An Indologist and linguist, Hermann Gundert earned his Ph.D. from the University of Tübingen (~1831–1835). He held posts with the Church Missionary Society (~1835–1838), the Basel Mission (1838), and as head of Calwer Verlag (1860).

Working in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies, Hermann Güntert earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg studying under Hermann Osthoff and Christian Bartholomae. He held professorships at the University of Rostock (1921) and Heidelberg University (1917; 1926–1945).

An Indologist and linguist, Hermann Hirt studied at Freiburg and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, August Leskien, and others, completing his PhD and Habilitation. He was a Privatdozent at Leipzig (1891–1912) and professor at Giessen (1912–1936).

Active in history, archaeology, and linguistics, Hermann Hunger studied at the universities of Vienna (~1960–1963), Heidelberg (~1964–1965), and Münster (~1965–1966). He held posts at the German Archaeological Institute, University of Chicago, and University of Vienna (1978–2007).

Specializing in religious studies and linguistics, Hermann Hupfeld studied at the University of Marburg (~1813–1817) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1822–1824). He subsequently held posts at Marburg (~1825–1843) and Halle-Wittenberg (~1843–1866).

An Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar, Hermann Jacobi studied at Berlin and Bonn under Johann Gildemeister. He served as a professor at the University of Münster (1876–1885) and the University of Bonn (1889–1922).

Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Hermann Kopp studied at Leipzig, the Walleser-Institut, and Heidelberg under Max Walleser and Heinrich Zimmer. He held directorships at the Walleser-Institut (1954–1958), Mainz Academy (1959–1964), and Heidelberg University (1964).

An Indologist, Hermann Kreyenborg studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1910–1914) and the University of Münster (1910–1921, Ph.D.) under Richard Schmidt. He served as a librarian at the University and State Library of Münster from 1922 to 1954.
